title: Implement a Post Tagging System for VitalPress CMS
description: This task requires implementing a full-stack feature for the VitalPress CMS: a content tagging system. This will allow administrators to categorize posts with keywords (tags), improving content organization and discoverability. The implementation will span multiple sessions, starting with the database and model layer, moving to the service logic, and finally exposing the feature through the controller/API layer. This tests the agent's ability to plan and execute a feature incrementally, retaining context between development sessions.

project_spec.name: VitalPress CMS
project_spec.description:
VitalPress CMS is a lightweight, security-focused content-management system written in C that enables small medical practices and community clinics to publish, manage and search patient-facing educational material (e.g., discharge instructions, preventive-care articles, medication guides) through a secure web portal. The system embraces a healthcare-centric feature set: built-in validation rules ensure every uploaded PDF or image complies with predefined HIPAA-safe MIME types; an SSL-first configuration and audit-grade logging safeguard protected health information; and an email-notification workflow immediately alerts staff when new content is published or revised, reducing the risk of outdated clinical guidance reaching patients.

Internally, VitalPress follows a strict layered architecture. At the lowest layer, a data-access module (SQLite) persists articles, version metadata and cached search indexes. The next layer hosts domain services—medical-taxonomy tagging, ICD-10 keyword extraction, and attachment virus scanning—exposed through a REST API. The presentation layer implements an MVC pattern served by GNU libmicrohttpd, with Authentication Middleware enforcing role-based access: clinicians, editors, and public visitors. Caching of rendered fragments is handled via libmemcached, speeding up anonymous patient access while keeping clinician dashboards fresh. Comprehensive error-handling funnels all faults to a centralized logger that can emit syslog, JSON or email alerts, providing the observability that healthcare compliance audits demand.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd (embedded HTTP server to expose REST endpoints and MVC views)
SQLite3 (lightweight relational storage for articles, revision history and user accounts)
cJSON (fast JSON serialization for REST API payloads)
OpenSSL (TLS/SSL termination and cryptographic utilities for password hashing and token signing)
libmemcached (object and fragment caching for high-read public content)
libmagic / file(1) signatures (server-side validation of uploaded file types and MIME safety checks)
libclamav (optional antivirus hook for file uploads)
libesmtp or sendmail interface (SMTP client for email notifications)
zlib (compression for static asset delivery and cached objects)
